routes.label: at a Civil Registry Authority office (cards personalised in a few city offices)

note: Landinfo's thematic note (updated 27 June 2022): the identity card is issued by the Civil Registry Authority; by law every Yemeni citizen must carry it (or a family book, as head of family) after turning 16, and the Civil Registry Law of 1991 (art. 52 a) sets its term at ten years, though cards seen in practice show about six. Both governments' offices issue it, and the recognised government accepts cards issued in Houthi-held areas. The fee and the time weren't found.

sources.title: Landinfo, Jemen: Sivilregister, identitetsdokumenter og pass (temanotat, updated 27 June 2022)
sources.said: ID-kort utstedes av Sivilregistermyndigheten. ... Ifølge loven skal ID-kortene utstedes med en gyldighet på ti år (Sivilregisterloven 1991, art. 52 a). ... Alle jemenittiske borgere skal ifølge loven bære ID-kort eller en familiebok (familiekort), dersom vedkommende er familieoverhode, etter fylte 16 år
